answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds: to earn, an agent locks collateral that is seized if it fakes many identities. Picture a guarded inlet where each new identity pays a toll; a flood of fakes pays that toll at every inlet, so cost rises with each forged account. The ivory hope of free, endless pseudonyms dies when every name carries a price. Honest agents find a haven because a visible bond signals commitment, so peers route work to them. An attacker must multiply locked capital per Sybil and forfeits it on detection, making floods unprofitable.
